findings.message: sources: The three named dimensions and their contents are not Dean's. docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:40 says she argued for three interlinked dimensions with lists (deliberation, peaceful conflict resolution, critical media literacy; social justice, equal dignity, pluralism). In the full paper 'dimension', 'civic knowledge', 'civic skills', 'media literacy', 'deliberat' and 'conflict resolution' all return zero hits; 'pluralis' hits only a reference-list title. What Dean does write: effective citizens need a body of knowledge, relevant skills, values and dispositions, and first-hand experience; the abstract names skills (problem-solving, decision-making) and values (civic mindedness, critical consciousness). Dependent items: docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:37, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:111, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:124, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:151. Repair: restate Dean's actual formulation, or attribute the three-part framework to a source that states it and verify; keep MCQ 2 only if reworded to what she wrote.

sources: docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:82 opens 'Dean (2005) put it clearly' and attributes 'primary agents of civic formation' and a statement that nation building in education is not indoctrination. Zero hits for 'primary agent', 'civic formation', 'collaborative inquiry', 'indoctrinat' and 'nation building' in the paper. Her nearest sentence is that the teacher is 'essential to the reconceptualization of education for democratic citizenship'. docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:40 also lists government departments, historical dates and constitutional bodies as what pupils memorised; none of those terms occurs as a memorised-content claim. Transmission teaching, rote memorisation and passive citizenship are supported, so that core stands. Repair: rewrite both passages to what the paper says and remove 'put it clearly'.

sources (constitutional accuracy): Article 251 is taught as protecting provincial languages at docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:70, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:96, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:119, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:22, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:127, docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:129 and the fig-U7-3 label ('provincial languages protected by Article 251'). Clause (3) is permissive: a Provincial Assembly 'may by law prescribe measures' for teaching, promotion and use, without prejudice to the national language. It creates no protection unless a province legislates. The provision that does give a right, Article 28 (any section of citizens with a distinct language, script or culture may preserve and promote it, subject to Article 251), is never mentioned. Sajid's reply to Zainab is also wrong on its own terms, since a village dialect is not a provincial language under 251(3). RRQ 5 (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:89) builds the error into its stem. Repair: teach 251(3) as a permission, add Article 28, and correct the figure, model answers and summaries.

sources (constitutional accuracy): docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:90 derives 'law applies to everyone, including the accused until proven otherwise' from Article 5(2). Article 5(2) states the obligation to obey the Constitution and law and says nothing about the accused. Fair treatment sits in Article 4 and Article 10A. Repair: cite those articles for that half of the sentence.

assessment: Two ERQ rubrics score criteria their stems do not ask for. ERQ 2 (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:99) asks for Dean and an example, but docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:154 awards 3 of 12 marks for using an article. ERQ 3 (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:100) never asks for an article or a reflection question, but docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:160 and docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/unit-assessment.mdx:162 score both (the Topic 7.1 summative task does ask for the article). A learner who answers the question as set loses marks. Repair: align stems and rubrics.

pedagogy: The anchor scenario is incoherent (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:24). In a government boys school, 'a third pupil, Zainab' is 'visiting the class with her teacher-education college', so she is both a pupil and a visiting trainee, and she is later answered as a pupil of the class (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:96). The topic's closing return to the scenario depends on her. Repair: give her one coherent role, for example a boy in the class or a co-educational school.

coverage: 'Constitutional values' is a spec key term and the object of the Create task, yet it is never defined (used at docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:100 and in the task). The activity requires 'the value and the article that carries it' and offers equal citizenship, mutual respect and the rule of law, but the unit gives no article for equal citizenship (Article 25 is never named) or the rule of law as such (Article 4 is never named). Repair: define the term and map each offered value to an article.

accessibility: fig-U7-1 overprints its own label. The text 'practice feeds the value' is centred at x=698 and the dashed return path runs vertically at x=690 through the same y, so the line strikes through the word 'feeds' in any font (see evidence/fig-U7-1.sharp.png). The label also ends close to the 780 viewBox edge. Repair: move the label clear of the path and re-run measure-figure-text, which could not run here.

authority/coverage, owner ruling needed: the guide's Week 15 title is 'Role of Education in Strengthening Ideology and Constitution' and the course description names 'strengthening national ideology'. The topic asks about ideology once (docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:32) and then never teaches it: Objectives Resolution, Article 2A and Article 31 are absent. Meanwhile Dean's central finding, that curriculum and textbooks do not distinguish Islamic education from citizenship education and promote exclusionary citizenship, is omitted, though it bears directly on ideology and integration and sits uneasily with the unit's framing. The three leaf sub-topics are taught, so I do not rule this a scope failure. Whether and how to treat this in a teacher-education text is an academic and sensitive judgement for the owner, not for this reviewer or an author alone.

sources: docs/semester-3/gicp-400/unit-07/topic-01.mdx:38 says 'His lesson for a country like Pakistan is that schools must deliberately create' active citizenship, 'not leave it to chance'. Kennedy addresses strategies for nation states, not schools. His only Pakistan mention is a quotation about states keeping their grip on citizenship education to induct the young into state culture and values, which is a different and more critical point. The abstract-level claims earlier in the paragraph are supported. Repair: mark the sentence as this unit's inference or reword it.

accessibility: No browser, narrow-view or A4 print inspection was possible because the crew brief forbids a build, dev server and Playwright, so reading order, table scrolling, figure captions, print layout and dark variants are unverified, and measure-figure-text (Chromium) was not run. The sharp previews used substituted colours and a fallback font and are not page renders. Literal SVGs render solid black under librsvg because it does not resolve the CSS var() colours; 96 sibling figures in units 1-6 share the pattern and all 14 variables resolve, so this looks like a tool limit and not a unit defect, but a browser has not confirmed it.
